notes: RecGym = gym-workout human activity recognition dataset. Sensing unit = 6-axis IMU (accel A_x,A_y,A_z + gyro G_x,G_y,G_z) plus a single-channel Body Capacitance sensor (C_1). Sampling rate 20 Hz. Worn at THREE positions: wrist, pocket, calf. 10 volunteers, each 5 sessions over 5 days (~1h/session). 12 activity classes: 11 workouts (Adductor, ArmCurl, BenchPress, LegCurl, LegPress, Riding, RopeSkipping, Running, Squat, StairsClimber, Walking) + a 'Null' class for time between workouts. Dataset DOI (UCI): 10.24432/C5PW4K. Dataset mirrors: UCI dataset/1128, Kaggle (zhaxidelebsz/10-gym-exercises-with-615-abstracted-features), GitHub github.com/zhaxidele/Toolkit-for-HBC-sensing (Data/GymData), project page zhaxidele.github.io/RecGym. Paper's key HBC finding: capacitive sensing beats single wrist accelerometer on leg-only exercises (0.89 vs 0.78 F1) and improves collaborative-activity recognition by ~16%. The arXiv 2210.14794 preprint (2022) is the paper the UCI page attributes the dataset to; no separate published DOI/journal-ref found on arXiv.
